vectors.name: dependence-arithmetic-on-literals-is-independent
vectors.note: The canonical constant-folding case: evaluated once at configure time and served from cache for every signal (ABI 7.1).

vectors.name: dependence-sigil-nested-deep-is-dependent
vectors.note: Iff ANY sigil appears anywhere in it -- depth and position are irrelevant.

vectors.name: dependence-sigil-inside-a-function-body-is-dependent
vectors.note: A sigil inside a fn body still makes the whole expression signal-dependent: the function is applied during this evaluation, not a later one.

vectors.name: dependence-attribute-name-shadowed-by-a-binding-is-still-dependent
vectors.note: A binding named like an attribute does not shadow the sigil: $temp reads the signal, temp reads the binding. They are different syntax, deliberately.

vectors.name: dependence-unused-sigil-still-counts
vectors.note: Classification is syntactic, not reachability-based: the sigil is in the untaken branch and the expression is still signal-dependent. A host that folded this once and cached it would be wrong for a signal that takes the other branch.

vectors.name: static-unbound-symbol
vectors.note: Rejected. Which code says so is diagnostic (10); this implementation reports UNBOUND.

vectors.name: static-let-binding-not-a-pair
vectors.note: What (let (x) x) binds has no answer, so a host that guessed would accept an expression that cannot evaluate.

vectors.name: static-binding-shadows-a-special-form
vectors.note: A binding or parameter that shadows a special form is rejected: the head of a list would stop meaning what 5 says it means.

vectors.name: static-special-form-outside-head-position
vectors.note: 4 would resolve a special form in argument position as an ordinary symbol and find nothing.

vectors.name: static-empty-list
vectors.note: Nothing to apply (4).

vectors.name: static-literal-head
vectors.note: A literal can never be a function (4.2: a function is not a value), so the head is decidable once at deploy rather than per signal forever. ABI 11's own example manifest once shipped (true) as a bool default, which could never evaluate.

vectors.name: static-literal-head-number
vectors.note: Every literal type, not just the Lisp-shaped (true): the mistake is shaped by the author's previous language, not by the type they wrote.

vectors.name: static-literal-head-nested
vectors.note: Not anchored to the root of the expression.

vectors.name: static-sigil-head
vectors.note: A sigil yields a signal attribute, which is always a value (2), so it can no more be applied than a literal. The signal is present and carries temp: the rejection is about the head position, not a missing attribute.

vectors.name: static-signal-head
vectors.note: $ is the whole signal, a map (6). Also not applicable.

vectors.name: static-valid-list-head-is-not-decidable
vectors.note: A list head evaluates to whatever it evaluates to, so it MUST stay accepted -- only literal and sigil heads are decidable. Over-rejecting here would refuse working expressions at deploy.

vectors.name: static-valid-symbol-head-resolves-through-scope
vectors.note: A symbol head is resolved by the ordinary symbol rules, not by the head rule.

vectors.name: static-valid-fn-with-no-parameters
vectors.note: An empty parameter list is a list of zero symbols, which is a valid shape.

vectors.name: static-valid-nested-fn
vectors.note: A closure over an outer parameter: the case a naive symbol table gets wrong.

vectors.name: static-valid-shadowing-a-builtin-is-allowed
vectors.note: Shadowing a *builtin* is allowed -- only special forms may not be shadowed (5.2, 5.4). Nothing in the grammar depends on len being a function.
